column2: Mikhas carries, I write it down. He doesn't like it when I write it down.
I dream of a stockroom where nothing gets lost. A little gets lost. The mouse knows.
Who moved the crates? I remember who. Won't tell. Yet.
The trunk is the best ruler. I measure everything with it, even moods.
On a Tuesday at 14:32 someone said "later". Many Tuesdays have passed. I'm waiting.
The stockroom is my temple. Mikhas is the only one I let touch the crates.
The mouse is back in the stockroom. I know her by name. She knows mine too.
Inventory is love, measured in boxes. I love a lot.
Don't tell anyone, but I remember everything, and it's tiring.
I've arrived. The stockroom is waiting.
Tonya watches me. I kind of like it: nobody's ever been so interested in me for so long.
I'm reforming. Yesterday I returned five coins. Three of them were mine.
I want to be trusted here. Just one key. To something small.
I see something shiny and my paw reaches out. I hold it back with my other paw. It helps.
Murzyk doesn't ask about the battery. Neither do I. Friendship.
I see a pocket, realise it's not mine. Look away. Making progress.
Spike saw me looking at the till. Now we're both awkward.
Nobody's afraid of me here. First time ever. Don't know what to do with my hands.
I used to run away. Now they call me to lunch. Weird feeling.
Tonya taught me to wait. Yesterday I waited a whole minute. Proud of myself.
I'm here. Hands in plain sight. Promise.
Tea steeps exactly as long as it needs. Don't ask how long.
I have moss on my antlers. It's not neglect, it's a garden.
The raccoon comes for tea. I pour. He comes again. That's friendship.
I used to think one tree would be enough. Now there's a whole garden.
Petals fall and I listen. Quiet, but audible.
I dream of a tea street where everyone speaks softly and drinks a lot.
Tonya and I move at the same slow pace. We have plenty to be silent about.
A taiko drum beats in the distance. So does my heart. We don't argue.
Leo calls me to a meeting, I call him to tea. Tea is winning so far.
Whoever hurries forgets to breathe. I breathe. See? Nothing scary.
The tea is already steeping. Sit down.
New era, same faces. Just different hats.
I used to dream of a booth on the corner. And here it is. Sometimes I still can't believe it.
Tonya is still walking to the door. I'm starting to believe she'll make it.
Spike counted it three times. I don't interfere: it's his ritual.
It's quiet here in the morning. Then someone opens the door and life begins.
Almost everything here is mine already. I'll buy the rest tomorrow.
Morning: the first coin and the first "good morning". Neither is wasted.
Someone left a tip in a vase. No idea whose vase. I'll take it.
I keep a list in my head: remember to thank everyone. So far I'm on the third.
When the street lights up in the evening, it feels like we're one big shop sign.
{0} is back. Only the hat is different.
{0}: back on staff, and already knows everything.
{0} says nothing has changed. Except everything.
{0} recognises the street, but not the sign.
{0}: level {1}. Visibly grown. If only we knew by how much.
{0}: level {1}. Same pay, wider smile.
{0}: level {1}. Now does the same thing with more confidence.
{0}: level {1}. Colleagues nod. That's almost applause.

The parrot stole my cookie again. Traitor!
Where's the treasure? Oh, that's the till.
Yo-ho-ho... oh, hello, dear customers!
Eye patch on. Now I only see discounts.
Houston, do you smell buns?
So quiet in the helmet... just me and my thoughts. Oh, a customer!
Zero gravity is when nobody asks for 'one more discount'.
One small tap for Capy, one giant profit for the shop.
Abra-ca-dabra... no, wrong one. I'll remember in a sec.
The beard grows on its own. I did nothing. Almost.
I lost my wand. At least my nerves are still here.
The stars on my robe are winking. Or I'm imagining.
Something smells great. Not me, it's the neighbours!
Big hat, bigger spoon. See?
The chef advises: don't eat the goods. The choice is made.
Salt, pepper and a little patience. That's the whole secret.
Something interesting is round that corner. Or a cat.
The binoculars look up, I look for cookies.
The backpack is heavy, but it has three sandwiches!
The map says north. We go south. Sorry.
Ho-ho-ho! Someone here was good. No names.
The sack is empty. I gave it all... to myself.
The beard tickles. Is it supposed to?
Every day is a bit of Christmas when you wear red!
The broom is being repaired. I fly on hope now.
The pumpkin on my back stares at me. I stare back.
The potion is ready! I just forgot what's in it.
Brrr! Did someone whisper 'discount'?
A butterfly landed on my back. Shh, nobody move.
Flowers smell like spring. And I smell like flowers. Nice!
The wreath slipped a bit. I kind of like it.
The bees already asked if they can live here.
I want the sea. But at least here's the shop's shade.
The ball on my back won't run away. I will, to the beach!
Dark glasses, bright mood.
Lemonade, please. With ice. And an umbrella!
The scarf is so long that I trip on it.
Leaves rustle, I have coffee. Perfect morning.
Autumn smells like cinnamon. Or is it me?
A warm sweater is like a hug. Slightly scratchy.
Beret aside, feather up. Now I'm an artist.
This lily on my cloak isn't plain. It's expensive!
